$note: Written after rendering the reel and looking at full-resolution stills from it — not from the contact sheet, which is an overview and not an inspection. Scores are one person's judgement out of ten and are deliberately NOT computed: every reel this repo has shipped broken passed the computed gates.
question: How Does the Human Heart Pump Blood?
verdict: This is the episode that once produced a gear train as a picture of a heart, and the one this phase changed most. Two builds ago the four chambers were grey discs on a bright ochre wash — every check passed them and the brightest thing in the frame was the empty air. The ground is pulled down behind the drawing now and the muscle takes the arterial colour rather than the plate's neutral, so it reads as tissue. Thirty causal links, the most of the five: the chambers contract on their own phases and the particles move because they do.
whatWorked: Flesh is the clearest demonstration that a material needs a body value: the same geometry went from grey buttons to tissue with one table change.
Blue leaves for the lungs, red comes back and goes out to the body and round again, and the circuit closes.
The chamber count is read off the sentence, not off the topic.
whatFailed: Four equal circles in a two-by-two grid labelled UPPER/UPPER/LOWER/LOWER is a circuit diagram, not a heart, and at a glance it reads as a face.
The caption names the right atrium while the drawing says UPPER — the vocabulary does not meet in the middle.
The valve marks are a few pixels tall; the one-way claim is carried by the caption more than by the drawing.

remainingDefects.what: The chamber layout is schematic to the point of abstraction
remainingDefects.why: honest, declared, and still the weakest read of the five
